trainingModes: untrained (train=false throughout: isolates the raw circuit/signal effect, no FdbLearning plasticity)
trained (single-v1 FdbLearning plasticity on top of the fixed graph+bias, 80 training + 40 held-out episodes)
protocol.bootstrap: paired by seed, resampled with replacement, B=10000, 95% percentile interval
conditions: direct-calibrated (ballast-90 core + symmetric deltaW calibrated to match relay's output16 Hz)
relay (functional-90: same core + 4-edge two-hop relay, zero deltaW bias)

question: Package A found that functional-90 (a 4-edge two-hop relay) beats ballast-90 on most tasks. Is that because the relay delivers more raw signal to the correct output neuron, or because of something structural/temporal about the two-hop path that an equally-strong one-hop boost cannot replicate?

calibration.method: 200-trial average output16 firing rate under a single cue0 (500Hz, 30ms) stimulation, no learner, no training. Direct deltaW found by 24-step bisection on [0,30] applied symmetrically to existing edges 0->16/0->17/1->16/1->17 via GraphDelta.addWeightDelta, matching relay's output16 Hz under the same stimulus. Matching assumed symmetric for cue1/output17 by construction (identical relay weights and identical deltaW on both sides) -- not independently verified for output17.

limitations: Host CPU fixtures. Calibration matches only output16 under cue0; output17/cue1 match relies on the fixture's built-in symmetry, not independently measured. Only one calibration point (500Hz, 30ms, the standard episode stimulus) is used; a different stimulus intensity could shift the Hz-matching deltaW. 20 seeds, not corrected for multiple comparisons across 2 training modes x 6 tasks x 3 pairwise contrasts = 36 comparisons.
